headline.name: round-0 drift (median key time rel. to key median)

findings.severity: blocking for the claim statement as worded (not for RESULTS.md)
findings.requirement: reporting contract: what a range is a range of
findings.finding: The statement's ranges 0.70-0.88 / 0.71-0.89 (2^24), 0.79-0.95 / 0.74-0.94 (2^28), 1.05-1.18 / 1.01-1.15 (2^32), the fast/std 4-11% / 0-15% and the BSGS 1.41-1.62x are ranges of cell medians (median over the 4 configurations of each (size, T) cell). The statement never says so and sets them beside per-configuration counts ('faster in 12 of 12 configurations'), so they read as per-configuration ranges. Per configuration the IC/rho ratio is 0.70-0.98 (std) / 0.70-0.97 (fast) at 2^24, 0.77-0.99 / 0.72-0.98 at 2^28 and 1.03-1.19 / 1.00-1.17 at 2^32; IC fast/std 0.82-0.98, rho fast/std 0.81-1.07, IC/BSGS 1.31-1.67. The statement also drops the disclosure the validated predecessor carried: each cell decision is a 4-of-4 sign rule (the bootstrap interval of a median of 4 equals their range). RESULTS.md labels its table 'median of 4 per cell' and gives the per-configuration ranges, so RESULTS itself is correct.
findings.amendment: say 'cell medians (median over the 4 configurations of each size-T cell)' and state the 4-of-4 sign rule; see claim-report.json proposed_wording

findings.severity: blocking for the claim statement as worded
findings.finding: The statement gives the fast build's 2^32 result as '1.01-1.15x (fast; 11 of 12 above 1)' without saying that the T = 1024 cell is unranked under the protocol rule (median 1.011, interval [0.996, 1.031]); only 2 of the 3 fast-build 2^32 cells are slower. RESULTS.md states it.
findings.amendment: '1.01-1.15 (fast; slower in 2 cells, unranked at T = 1024; 11 of 12 configurations above 1)'

findings.finding: RESULTS says 'load average 40-89' (twice). The 1-minute load average recorded at each of the 3672 executions spans 37.6-93.5; 40 and 89 are the medians of the last and first sixths of the run (39.9, 89.1). Per round the median is 86.6, 77.3, 61.0.
findings.amendment: '1-minute load average 38-94 at the executions (medians 87, 77, 61 in rounds 1-3)'

findings.finding: 'the pinned CPU's SMT sibling was idle apart from the pod's own job server' is not supported by any recorded artifact: host.json records the cpuset (27, 56, 91, 120) and the pin (91) but no thread-sibling topology and no per-CPU utilisation, and a container's cpuset on a shared host is not evidence that other tenants do not run on those CPUs. That CPU 27 is 91's sibling is itself an assumption about the host's numbering.
findings.amendment: remove, or label as an assumption: 'the container's cpuset contained CPU 27, presumably 91's SMT sibling; its use by other tenants is not recorded'

findings.finding: Prediction 1 had a magnitude clause ('magnitudes within about 10% of the session VM's'); it fails in 4 of 9 cells (RunPod std / VM cell median: 24/1024 1.136, 24/16384 0.845, 28/1024 0.849, 28/4096 0.790). The outcome column says 'holds in direction' and does not say the magnitude clause failed. Prediction 2's per-arm figures are not evaluated: median fast/std key time over 36 configurations ic5rw 0.85 (predicted about 0.6), ic5ks 0.84 (about 0.8: holds), ic5 0.93 and ic5w 0.93 (0.94-0.96: about holds), rhodpu 0.98 (changes little: holds), rho2xks 0.84 (a rho arm gaining as much as ic5ks; not predicted).
findings.amendment: outcome of prediction 1: 'direction holds; the magnitude clause fails in 4 of 9 cells (up to 21% from the VM, 28 b T = 4096)'; prediction 2: list the per-arm outcomes

findings.finding: (a) 'slower in 12 of 12 at 2^32 (1.03-1.20x)': the largest configuration ratio is 1.19497, i.e. 1.19. (b) 'Fastest arms: rho side rho2xks at 24 b ... and rhodpu elsewhere': in the fast build at 28 b T = 1024 rho2xks is the fastest rho in 1 of 4 configurations.
findings.amendment: '1.03-1.19x'; 'rhodpu elsewhere (rho2xks in 1 of 4 configurations at 28 b T = 1024 in the fast build)'

findings.finding: (a) The A/A noise figure 'median |log(repeat/median)| over all keys is 0.008' is computed as stated, but with 3 repeats one term per key is the median itself (exactly 0), so a third of the terms are zero; over the two non-median repeats the median is 0.020 (95th percentile 0.12). (b) 'The IC/rho effects at 2^24 (12-30%) and 2^32 (5-20%) are larger than the drift': at 2^32 the fast build's T = 1024 cell is 1.011 (1%), not larger than the ~3% drift; and '5-20%' combines the std cell medians (5-18%) with a per-configuration maximum (19.5%).
findings.amendment: report 0.020 (non-median repeats) beside 0.008; 'at 2^32 5-18% (std) and 1-15% (fast) by cell median; the fast build's 2^32 T = 1024 cell (1%) is within the drift'

findings.finding: launch.py builds the payload with tarfile mode 'w:gz', whose gzip header carries time.time(); the docstring's 'deterministic' holds for the tar stream only. The pinned payload is reproduced bit for bit from the committed run.py, the 12 instances and the validator's rebuilt binaries with gzip mtime 1794501148 (16:32:28Z), found by search in the window 14:29:44Z-16:32:35Z; attempt 1's pin d44404ff... is likewise reproduced from fde73fb405's run.py (mtime found by search). The rows carry no commit field (runs.json commit [null]); the binding is bin_sha256 -> launch/payload.json -> commit, closed here by the bit-identical rebuild.
findings.amendment: pass mtime=0 to the gzip writer in future payloads; record the source commit in host.json

findings.finding: No pod token in any commit fde73fb405^..51ca1eb6d6 (attempt 2's token checked by value with git grep and pickaxe; attempt 1's token is not available to the validator, and no 48-hex string occurs in any study file; every long hex string there is a 64-hex sha256). create.json keeps only env key names. The receipts do commit the RunPod consumerUserId and machineId (account and host identifiers, not credentials).
